 Ready to reduce bus fares if Centre cuts petrol, diesel prices: CM DK Shivakumar
 The CM defended the fare hike, citing mounting losses of state-run transport corporations and the financial burden of the Shakti scheme. He also clarified that variations in milk prices are due to differences in quality and fat content. 
 Moneycontrol News 
 November 04, 2026 / 18:58 IST 
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 DK Shivakumar 
 Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar on November 4 said the state government is willing to consider reducing bus fares if the Centre lowers petrol and diesel prices.
 "If the Central Government reduces the prices of petrol and diesel, we are prepared to reduce bus fares in the state accordingly," Shivakumar told reporters at Vidhana Soudha on Wednesday.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Responding to the Opposition's call for a statewide protest on November 5 against the recent bus fare hike, CM defended the government's decision, citing the financial difficulties faced by the four state-run transport corporations.

 "The transport corporations are running at a loss. There was a situation when they did not even have sufficient funds to purchase diesel for the next 10 days to three weeks. The government had to step in and provide the necessary financial assistance," he said.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 He also pointed to the financial burden imposed by Shakti scheme, which provides free bus travel to women on state-run non-AC buses.

 "Shakti scheme has placed an additional financial burden on the transport corporations. Consequently, fares may have been increased by Rs 2 or Rs 3 on certain routes," he said.
 Karnataka government on November 4 announced an average fare hike of 35 percent for the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) and 23 percent for Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) and other two state-run transport corporations. The revised fares will come into effect from November 5.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Questioning the Opposition's protests, Shivakumar asked why political parties had remained silent when prices of essential commodities and fuel were increased.
 "Why did the Opposition parties remain silent when petrol and diesel prices were increased? Why did they not raise their voices when cooking gas prices went up? Why did they not protest against the increase in the prices of fertilisers, pesticides, steel, cement and medicines? Are they not concerned about the rising cost of agricultural inputs and the burden it places on farmers?" he asked.
 The CM said the government was aware of the difficulties faced by farmers amid the ongoing drought in the state but maintained that the transport corporations also needed financial support to remain viable.
 "I am fully aware of the hardships faced by farmers during the ongoing drought in the state. We understand their difficulties and struggles. At the same time, the transport corporations must also remain financially viable. They must be given an opportunity to recover from their financial difficulties," he said.
 He challenged Opposition parties to urge Prime Minister Narendra Modi to reduce the taxes and cesses levied on petrol and diesel.
 CM clarifies on milk price hike 
 Shivakumar also clarified reports that milk prices had increased by Rs 12 per litre in some places, instead of the announced Rs 8 per litre hike.
 He said the variations in prices were due to differences in milk quality and fat content.
 "All milk is not the same. Regular milk, milk from indigenous cows and buffalo milk are different varieties. Their fat content also varies. People need to understand these differences," he said.
